question: The dimensions of force are:
solution:
The correct answer is [M L T⁻²]. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The dimensions of **force** are typically represented as **[M L T⁻²]** because force is directly proportional to **mass and acceleration**, and acceleration is represented as** [L T⁻²].**
 
• According to physics, a **force** is an influence that, in the absence of other forces, has the capacity to cause an object to change **its velocity, or accelerate.**
 
• The everyday idea of **pushing or pulling** is made mathematically by the concept of force.
 
• [M0 L3 TO] = Dimensional formula for volume.
 
• [M L-3 T0] = Dimensional formula for density.
 
• [M0 L T-1] =Dimensional formula for speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"dimensions**" in this context refers to the** fundamental physical quantities **that are used to describe a particular **physical quantity.**
 
• **[M¹ L² T**⁻**²****]** represents the dimensions of** torque**, which is the twisting force that causes rotation.
 
 
• The source of an **angular acceleration** is torque.
 
• Thus, torque can be thought of as** linear force's rotating equivalent.**
 
 
 
• **[M¹ L⁻¹ T⁻²****]** represents the dimensions of** pressure**, which is the force applied perpendicular to a surface per unit area.
 
 
• The International System of Units (SI) uses the** Pascal** (Pa) as the measure of **pressure or stress.**
 
 
 
• **[M0 L¹ T-1] **represents the dimensions of **velocity,** which is the rate of change of position with respect to time.
 
 
• In kinematics, the area of classical mechanics that studies how bodies **move**, velocity is a** basic idea. **
